newsitem.title: USA: On-line campaign debate focuses on children.
newsitem.headline: On-line campaign debate focuses on children.

text.p: Representatives of the three major presidential campaigns debated children's issues in a live discussion on America OnLine Tuesday.
The debate, which ran from 8 p.m. to 9 p.m. EST, focused on children's issues such as child care, early childhood education, special students' needs and alleviating childhood poverty.

Sponsored by the Coalition for America's Children, Moms Online, the Casey Journalism Center and Kidscampaigns, the event allowed parents, children's advocates, the media and the public to question the candidates' representatives.
Sharon Robinson, assistant secretary of education, spoke for President Clinton's campaign, stressed urban initiatives, hiring of quality teachers and intense community involvement.
Sen. Don Nickles, R-Oklahoma, represented Republican Bob Dole, advocating school vouchers that would give parents more freedom to choose where their children attend schoool.
Russell Verney, campaign director for Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, suggested that children should start school before the age of six.
